name: AD9280ARSZRL
title: AD9280: 8-bit, 32 MSPS, 95 mW CMOS A/D converter
summary: A single-supply 8-bit pipelined ADC sampling at up to 32 MSPS, with its own sample-and-hold and a reference that can be set to 1 V, 2 V or anything between, or bypassed for an external one. It runs from 2.7 V to 5.5 V, uses 95 mW at 3 V and under 5 mW asleep, and drives a three-state straight-binary bus with an out-of-range flag. The input can be single-ended, centred on a chosen level or differential, an on-chip clamp restores the DC level of AC-coupled video, and the input stage reaches 300 MHz so IF signals up to 135 MHz can be undersampled. It drops into AD876-8 sockets.

circuits.title: Figure 17. Reference decoupling network
circuits.description: The network every configuration places on the force pins: a 10 µF and a 0.1 µF capacitor across REFTF and REFBF, and a 0.1 µF capacitor from each of the two pins to ground.

circuits.title: Figure 18. Internal reference, 1 V p-p input span (top/bottom mode)
circuits.description: Single-ended input from 0 V to 1 V. The internal reference runs in its 1 V setting with VREF tied to REFSENSE, VREF drives REFTS, and REFBS sits at ground. MODE at AVDD selects top/bottom operation. VREF carries 1.0 µF tantalum and 0.1 µF ceramic to ground.

circuits.title: Figure 19. Internal reference, 2 V p-p input span (top/bottom mode)
circuits.description: Single-ended input from 0 V to 2 V. REFSENSE at ground sets the internal reference to 2 V, VREF drives REFTS, REFBS is grounded and MODE is at AVDD.

circuits.title: Figure 20. Internal reference, 1 V p-p input span (center span mode)
circuits.description: Single-ended input swinging 1 V p-p about 1.5 V, from 1 V to 2 V. REFTS and REFBS are tied together and held by a low-impedance 1.5 V source, VREF is tied to REFSENSE for a 1 V span, and MODE is driven to AVDD/2.

circuits.title: Figure 21. External reference mode, 1 V p-p input span
circuits.description: Input from 1 V to 2 V with the span set by two external sources: 2 V on REFTS and 1 V on REFBS, both low impedance. REFSENSE and MODE at AVDD turn the internal reference amplifier off and select top/bottom operation.

circuits.title: Figure 22. External reference mode, 1 V p-p input span, 2.5 V common mode
circuits.description: Input from 2.0 V to 3.0 V about 2.5 V. REFTS and REFBS, tied together, sit on the 2.5 V output of a REF43. A 1.5 kΩ over 1 kΩ divider from the 2.5 V node makes 1 V, filtered by 0.1 µF and buffered by an op amp (A3) wired as a follower into VREF. REFSENSE at AVDD disables the internal reference amplifier; MODE is at AVDD/2. The buffer must handle 10 kΩ plus capacitance.

circuits.title: Figure 23a. External reference, 2 V p-p input span
circuits.description: Input from 2 V to 4 V, compatible with the AD876. A low-impedance 4 V source drives REFTF with REFTS tied to it, and a 2 V source drives REFBF with REFBS tied to it. 10 µF and 0.1 µF sit across the two nodes and 0.1 µF from each to ground. REFSENSE is at AVDD, MODE at ground, VREF open.

circuits.title: Figure 23b. Kelvin connected reference
circuits.description: Two op amps drive the force pins and take their feedback from the sense pins, so the top and bottom references are held at the chip. The upper amplifier takes REFT on its + input, drives REFTF, and senses REFTS; the lower takes REFB, drives REFBF and senses REFBS. C4 and C5 (0.1 µF) join each sense line to its force line; C3 and C1 (0.1 µF) go from the force pins to ground; C2 (10 µF) and C6 (0.1 µF) sit across REFTF and REFBF.
notes: Lower amplifier output: its pin number 6 duplicates the upper amplifier's inverting input.

circuits.title: Figure 24b. Video clamp circuit
circuits.description: Pins for clamping an AC-coupled video signal: REFTF tied to REFTS and REFBF tied to REFBS, with 10 µF and 0.1 µF across them and 0.1 µF from each to ground; MODE at AVDD/2; a logic pulse train on CLAMP; CLAMPIN tied to REFBS or to an external DC level.

circuits.title: Figure 26. Simple drive configuration
circuits.description: A source drives AIN through a series resistor of under 20 Ω, which eases the load the switched-capacitor input puts on the source.

circuits.title: Figure 27. AC coupled input
circuits.description: VIN reaches AIN through C1 with C2 in parallel, then R1. R2 from the coupled node to a VBIAS source sets the DC level. The high-pass corner is set by R2 and C1 + C2; C1 is a large electrolytic or tantalum part and C2 a small ceramic or polystyrene part near 0.01 µF.

circuits.title: Figure 28. Bipolar level shift
circuits.description: An AD8041 shifts a ground-referenced 1 V p-p signal up to the ADC's input range. The signal and a midscale offset voltage each pass a resistor into the + input, which has a resistor to ground; the output feeds back to the - input through a resistor and drives AIN through 20 Ω. +VCC carries 0.1 µF to ground.

parts.value: signal, 1 V p-p about 0 V DC

circuits.title: Figure 29. Differential input
circuits.description: A transformer drives a 1 V p-p differential signal: one end of the secondary into AIN, the other into REFTS and REFBS tied together, and its center tap to AVDD/2. VREF is tied to REFSENSE for the 1 V reference; MODE is at AVDD/2.

circuits.title: Figure 30. AD876 mode
circuits.description: The pin strapping that lets the part sit in an AD876-8 socket: 4 V drives REFTF and REFTS, 2 V drives REFBF and REFBS, MODE is open, REFSENSE is at AVDD, CLAMP, CLAMPIN and OTR are tied to ground, and VREF has 0.1 µF to ground.

circuits.title: Figure 34. IF sampling circuit
circuits.description: Undersampling an IF signal. The SAW filter output, terminated in 50 Ω to ground, drives the first non-inverting stage directly (20 dB, 200 Ω over 22.1 Ω); a 50 Ω series resistor feeds the second (12 dB, 280 Ω over 93.1 Ω), and another 50 Ω feeds an L-C bandpass filter and a 1:4 transformer (Mini-Circuits T4-6T). The secondary, loaded by 200 Ω, drives AIN and REFTS with REFBS tied together, for differential operation with a 1 V span; its center tap sits at AVDD/2 from a 1 kΩ / 1 kΩ divider bypassed with 0.1 µF. VREF is tied to REFSENSE with 1.0 µF and 0.1 µF to ground.

circuits.title: Figure 16f. Variable reference, between 1 V and 2 V
circuits.description: Two external resistors set VREF anywhere from 1 V to 2 V: RA from VREF to REFSENSE and RB from REFSENSE to AVSS, giving VREF = 1 V × (1 + RA/RB). Fitting RA and RB switches the internal 10 kΩ resistors out. VREF carries 0.1 µF and 1.0 µF to ground.

operation.text: A pipeline of four sample-and-hold stages, each with its own coarse converter, DAC and gain, so the first stage takes a new sample while the later ones finish the three before it. Digital correction combines the stages; the result comes out three clock cycles after the sample. It needs far fewer comparators than the 256 of a flash design.

The pipeline uses both clock edges, so duty cycle matters: tCH and tCL are each 14.7 ns min. HC/HCT or AC/ACT CMOS logic is the recommended driver. The input threshold is near AVDD/2, so 3.3 V or 5 V CMOS swings both work. Clocking faster than 32 MSPS may work with lower performance; slower clocks can improve it slightly. Output buffer power is roughly proportional to clock rate.

While CLK is low the input tracks onto a hold capacitor through a 50 Ω switch; on the rising edge it holds. Pin and hold capacitance together are under 5 pF, and the source must settle this load to 8-bit accuracy within half a clock period. A series resistor of 20 Ω or less keeps specified performance; for signals under 16 MHz it can be raised in proportion. A shunt capacitor from AIN to analog ground also lowers the AC load.

REFTF and REFBF carry the references the converter actually uses and are always decoupled (Figure 17): 10 µF and 0.1 µF across them and 0.1 µF from each to ground. REFTS and REFBS are the sense inputs that set the span. VREF needs 1.0 µF tantalum in parallel with 0.1 µF low-ESR ceramic to AVSS. The reference drives at most 1 mA; heavier loads need a buffer.

A bandgap and amplifier A1 give 1 V with REFSENSE tied to VREF, 2 V with REFSENSE grounded, or 1 V to 2 V with a resistor divider from VREF to REFSENSE to ground. Both 1 V and 2 V settings work on 3 V and 5 V supplies. The 2 V span gives the best noise; the 1 V span gives the best distortion.

REFSENSE tied to AVDD turns A1 off. Then either VREF is driven, or REFTS and REFBS are driven directly to any levels within the supply 1 V to 2 V apart. Internal buffer A2 means an external source only has to drive 10 kΩ. In AD876-compatible use REFTF/REFTS and REFBF/REFBS are driven together from low-impedance sources.

MODE at AVDD gives top/bottom operation, the input spanning REFBS to REFTS. MODE at AVDD/2 gives center span, with REFTS and REFBS shorted at the midscale voltage and the input swinging about it, or differential operation with AIN as one input and REFTS/REFBS shorted as the other; differential is best for distortion. For good high-frequency SINAD and SFDR single-ended, center the input near 1.5 V with REFTS/REFBS on a low-impedance 1.5 V source. MODE open or at AVSS gives AD876-8 compatible operation.

For AC-coupled inputs such as video, a high on CLAMP closes SW1 and an internal amplifier servos AIN to CLAMPIN; low opens it and CIN holds the level until the next pulse, drooping by the input bias current. Keep RIN at 10 Ω or more for the clamp loop's stability. CLAMPIN works from 0.5 V to 2.0 V. Size CIN for droop first, then the pulse width for acquisition; 1 µs to 3 µs suits most uses once CIN is charged. Example: video at 2 V to 3 V moved to a 1 V to 2 V span with CLAMPIN at 1 V (an external level or REFBS), pulsing during sync or back porch.

The switched input draws a net DC current that grows with sample rate and with the distance of the input from the reference midpoint (REFTS – REFBS)/2; Figure 14 gives it at 32 MHz. Through an AC-coupling network it makes an offset of (R1 + R2) × IB; a small R2 or an adjusted VBIAS compensates.
For DC coupling an op amp shifts a ground-referenced signal into the input range; Figure 28 uses an AD8041 non-inverting with a midscale offset voltage summed at its + input.
STBY high with the clock held low puts the converter to sleep at about 4 mW (under 5 mW). It wakes 400 ns typ after STBY returns low.

THREE-STATE, STBY and CLK are referenced to analog ground. Output coding is straight binary from –FS to +FS, with OTR going high beyond either end. THREE-STATE high puts the data bus in high impedance (tDHZ 13 ns, tDEN 25 ns typ), meant for in-circuit testing. Output drivers run from DRVDD: at 5 V they suit high-speed CMOS and F, AS and S TTL; at 3 V they keep 32 MSPS with low-voltage CMOS. A fan-out of one keeps the load under 20 pF.

In an AD876-8 socket the grounded REFSENSE and open MODE put the part into external reference mode, the socket's reference lands on the reference pins, and the clamp controls are grounded. Latency is 3 cycles against the AD876-8's 3.5.

With 300 MHz full-power bandwidth the part can alias an IF down to baseband, for example a 45 MHz IF sampled at 20 MSPS lands at 5 MHz (FS/4). An image-rejection bandpass filter ahead of it is needed. Figure 34 uses a transformer-fed differential input on a 1 V span whose center tap sits at midsupply, after a SAW filter, 32 dB of gain from one or two AD8009 amplifiers and an L-C bandpass filter that removes the amplifier's second-order products and out-of-band noise (the converter's noise bandwidth is over 220 MHz). The gain stage also isolates the SAW filter from the input's charge kickback. Figures 35 to 38 were taken with AVDD = 5 V, DRVDD = 3.3 V.

Use at least four layers with ground and power planes. Join analog and digital grounds in a solid plane directly under the part. Keep digital lines away from and not parallel to the input traces, and keep digital return currents out of the analog circuitry.

INL is each code's distance from a straight line from half an LSB below the first transition to 1.5 LSB beyond the last. DNL is how far each code width departs from 1 LSB. Offset error is how far the first transition sits from 1 LSB above zero. Gain error is how far the distance between first and last transitions departs from ideal. Latency is the clock count from sampling to the matching output; new data appears on every rising edge.
